sourceTitle: Goodman service manual RS6621003r3 (June 2020), 80% single-stage gas furnaces GMES80, AMES80, GCES80, ACES80, VMES80 and VCES80, troubleshooting chart
safetyNote: If you smell gas, do not touch any electrical switch or use a phone in the building; leave immediately and call your gas supplier from outside. Turn off electrical power at the furnace switch or breaker before opening any panel, and never bypass or jumper a limit, rollout or pressure switch. Gas valve, burner, venting, wiring and control-board work should be done by a licensed HVAC technician.
displayPattern: Diagnostic LED through the blower-door window on an 80% single-stage *MES80 or *CES80 furnace: Goodman GMES80 and GCES80, Amana AMES80 and ACES80, GMC VMES80 and VCES80. Count the flashes between pauses. This is not the 7-segment EE display on a 90%+ furnace.
meaning: Flame is sensed when the gas valve should be off. The induced draft blower and the circulator keep running.
causes: A short to ground in the flame-sense circuit
Miswiring, a lingering burner flame, or a gas valve that is slow to close, which the abnormal-operation section also lists for five flashes
diySteps: Turn the furnace off at its switch. If you smell gas, leave and call the gas supplier from outside
Do not leave the furnace running in this state
Technician: the chart says to correct a short at the flame sensor or in the flame-sensor wiring, with power off
proAdvice: Five flashes means the control sees flame with no call for heat. That can be a wiring short or a valve that is not closing. Call a licensed HVAC technician. This chart is service manual RS6621003r3 for those 80% single-stage models. A 7-segment code such as EE0 or EE2 is a different furnace family.
